summary: A 100-foot steel tower dated to 1937 in Ozark County; the Forest Service says it is no longer in use and not open to the public, while a news report says it still stands.

facts.design: Steel tower, 100 feet tall (per Central US Lookouts)
facts.status_note: A River Hills Traveler report says the tower stands on the hillside. The Forest Service says it is no longer in use and not open to the public.

access.note: The Forest Service says the old tower is no longer in use and not open to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The River Hills Traveler report says the tower stands on the hillside; the Forest Service says it is no longer in use and not open to the public. Both are reported. Neither source says the tower is in service, so the story does not describe it as open or in use.

notes_for_editor: The 1937 date and 100-foot height rest on one lookout history page. The Forest Service page is undated, and the River Hills Traveler article is undated. No staffing, fire or rental information was found in the cache. The brief's 30.5 m height matches the 100-foot figure. The NHLR and firetower.org pages were not in the cache. Two search hits (a Facebook group post about remaining tower structures, and anyplaceamerica and news-leader pages) were blocked or not fetchable and are not used.
